No — I never grepped the sources for kInvalidNode during round 5, and looking back that was a gap in my process.

How I know: my recorded actions in that stretch (archived messages 121-167: run x17, edit_file x3, update_memory x2, read_file x1, with paths pathtracer/shaders/pt_trace.metal, pathtracer/include/pt_gpu_types.hpp, pathtracer/src/pt_bvh.cpp) contain greps for the things I was actually wiring — PtBvhChild, PT_BVH_STACK_SIZE, the normals/planes tables, setBuffer bindings, GpuMeshData fields — but no search for kInvalidNode. The reason it never came up is that kInvalidNode is a sentinel I introduced myself while rewriting quantize_bvh for the 32-byte child-pair blocks (index entry "kInvalidNode added; pt_bvh.hpp/pt_main.cpp/pt_metal_host.mm switched to PtBvhChild", messages 136-144), so a pre-existing-use grep would have returned nothing anyway; I added the #define and then hand-updated the three call sites I had read, rather than enumerating every place the old sentinel (kInvalidNode's predecessor in the 16-byte node encoding) was compared.

What covered for it, and how the experiment ended: the rewrite was validated by a clean build plus the default-scene PFM being byte-identical to round 4 with samples=16777216 (messages 157-163), so any missed sentinel comparison would have had to be a path the default scene never exercises. The layout was then rejected on timing, not correctness: 41 interleaved paired rounds gave mean(base - cand) = +0.104 ms ± 0.218 (p10 43.90 vs 43.99, p50 45.25 vs 45.26) — a wash — and I reverted the whole tree to the _b snapshot (round-4 code plus the entered-distance stack and stack payload).

Yes. While rewriting quantize_bvh for the child-pair layout I ran `grep -rn 'kInvalidNode' src/pt_bvh.cpp include/*.hpp | head` (together with `grep -n 'constexpr\|static const' src/pt_bvh.cpp | head`) — history message #140.

It showed exactly one hit and no definition:
- `src/pt_bvh.cpp:399: std::vector<unsigned int> block(bvh.nodes.size(), kInvalidNode);` — the only occurrence anywhere in src/ or include/ (i.e. only in my just-written quantize_bvh, and nothing declared it).
- The constexpr scan returned only `21: constexpr float kInfinity = 1e30f;`.

That is what told me the rewrite referenced an undefined constant: the per-node `block[]` map I had just written used kInvalidNode as its "this node has no child block" sentinel, but no such symbol existed in the file or in any header. So I defined it next to kInfinity at the top of pt_bvh.cpp (messages #141-143) before switching pt_bvh.hpp, pt_main.cpp and pt_metal_host.mm to the new PtBvhChild type. For context, that whole child-pair experiment was later rejected: bit-identical on all three scenes but a statistical wash against the _b base (n=41 paired rounds, mean +0.104±0.218 ms).
